newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-DERBY WINNER SHAAMIT RETIRED.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DERBY WINNER SHAAMIT RETIRED.

text.p: Epsom Derby winner Shaamit has been retired after suffering an injury in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe horse race in France early this month.
"Shaamit has been retired after injuring a tendon," Darley Stud Management Company managing director Justin Wadham said in a statement on Wednesday.
"Fears that a knock received in the Forte Meridien Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe might have caused more damage than mere bruising were confirmed yesterday."
Wadham said plans for Shaamit's career as a stallion had not been finalised.
The three-year-old won the Derby in June this year, beating Dushyantor and subsequent St Leger winner Shantou into second and third respectively.
But he failed to win again after Epsom, his best effort being third behind Pentire and Classic Cliche in the Diamond Stakes at Ascot.
The news was a crushing blow for owner William Haggas.
"From a personal point of view, I am very upset and now we have got to find another star," he said. "We are only a small yard and are very sorry to lose him.
"It's such a pity because I said all along he would get better as he got older but no-one will be able to see that now."
